newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-firm - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-firm - dealers.

text.p: Midwest cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady to firm amid ideas that recent brisk pork sales would stimulate increased packer demand, livestock dealers said.
Top prices in Iowa and southern Minnesota for hogs delivered to the plant could range from $54.00 to $55.00 per cwt and Illinois top prices could range from $53.50 to $54.00.
Indiana and Ohio tops were seen at $52.50 to $53.00 at plants, dealers there said.
Prices also could be underpinned by ideas that supplies of market-ready animals were starting to tighten, they said.

Last week's estimated slaughter of 1.961 million hogs produced large supplies of pork, which in turn weighed on wholesale prices, sources said. As a result, the lower pork values may have sparked increased retail buying, they said.

USDA Tuesday reported 90.1 fabricated loads and 37.5 loads of pork trimmings had traded at lower prices. Market analysts said the total was nearly double the amount of loads normally sold on a Tuesday.
By midday Wednesday, an estimated 47.5 fabricated loads and 33 loads of trimmings had been sold, they said.
